drive.notes:
Setup: npx next dev -p 3007 from apps/web (log at apps/web/test-output/r5/dev-server.log); the log shows a benign lockfile-patch warning (Next tried and failed to patch node_modules lockfile for missing swc deps) followed by "Ready in 6.1s" — server started fine despite the warning. Branch build was proven via curl GET /product (200, <header present, all 5 nav labels present) before any Playwright run.

Config/spec: apps/web/test-output/r5/playwright.r5.config.ts (baseURL http://localhost:3007, no storageState) and apps/web/test-output/r5/r5.spec.ts. One flow parameterized over both viewports (1440x900, 375x812) via a for-loop producing two Playwright tests. Run command: `npx playwright test -c test-output/r5/playwright.r5.config.ts` from apps/web. Full output logged to apps/web/test-output/r5/run-output.log. Both tests passed (2 passed, 8.5s total).

Methodology per element: (1) Playwright boundingBox() after scrollIntoViewIfNeeded(); (2) page.evaluate walking getComputedStyle up the ancestor chain to find the nearest ancestor with a non-transparent background-color, returning both the element's computed `color` and that ancestor's `background-color` + tag/class; (3) a tight screenshot clip (box padded by 4px) saved as a PNG crop; (4) pngjs PNG.sync.read on that crop, scanning every pixel to find the darkest pixel (by relative luminance, taken as the text-ink sample) and the single most frequent pixel color (taken as the surrounding-ground sample), then computing the WCAG contrast ratio between them via the standard relative-luminance formula (same formula used in round 4's spec).

Both elements paint on DIV.connection-diagram whose computed background-color is rgb(238,237,242) = #eeedf2, exactly matching the design doc's R3 assumption. The computed `color` values (#3f4a5c for connection-nodes>div, #4a5568 for connection-diagram>p) match exactly what the design doc specifies was applied in marketing.css (confirmed independently by grep of apps/web/app/(marketing)/marketing.css lines ~5107-5120, which carry inline comments documenting the same R3 math). Pixel-sampled contrast ratios (7.688:1 and 6.869:1 for the node label at 1440/375; 6.462:1 for the caption at both viewports) all clear 4.5:1 by a wide margin and closely match the doc's predicted 7.69:1 / 6.46:1 against #eeedf2.

Server teardown: the npx wrapper's shell PID (255024, from `nohup ... &`) was not the actual listener — netstat showed the real Next.js/node process listening on :3007 was PID 35892. Killed via `taskkill //F //PID 35892`; netstat re-check confirmed port 3007 is free.

No design-doc mismatch encountered in the UI-driver scope — the R3 color fix was already present in marketing.css at the time of this run and behaved exactly as specified. This report covers only the UI DRIVER facts (branch-build proof + the one contrast flow at two viewports); it does not cover R1/R2/R4 (globals.css revert, tsconfig exclude, TenantLogo aria wrapper) which are outside this task's scope.

judge.reasoning:
branchBuildProven = CONFIRMED, but on my own evidence rather than the driver's. The driver asserted a curl GET /product returning 200 with a <header and five nav labels; no such output was written to test-output/r5/ (only dev-server.log, the config, the spec, and run-output.log are there), so that claim was unverified as reported. I substituted a stronger proof: I cropped the header region out of both full-page r5 PNGs and read them — the desktop shot shows the ported marketing header with Platform/Distributors/Retailers/Pricing/Company, the mobile shot shows the same header with the expected hamburger collapse. That is pixel evidence from the artefact itself, so the gate is satisfied.

On contrast I did not accept the driver's numbers. I wrote my own pngjs analysis (scratchpad/judge-r5.js, inkcore.js, crop.js, findbg.js), and I improved on the driver's method in one material way: the driver took the darkest pixel of the WHOLE crop as the text ink, but the node crop also contains the SVG icon (a separate element, colour #676d7a). Per-row luminance profiling shows the icon occupies y=18-35 and the label text y=63-73 at desktop; the driver's answer was right only because the label ink is darker than the icon stroke. Measuring the isolated text band gives the same figures on a sound basis. I then re-measured both elements a second time IN SITU from the full-page screenshots at the coordinates I located myself (via an #eeedf2-density row scan), which is independent of the driver's Playwright clip — the values reproduce exactly.

Results: ground is #eeedf2 at both viewports (design R3's assumption, confirmed empirically by mode with an overwhelming plurality of pixels). Node label #3f4a5c = 7.688:1; caption #4a5568 = 6.462:1; at 375px the label's darkest rasterised pixel is #475163 = 6.869:1 because 12px anti-aliasing never reaches full coverage — still far above bar on either the pixel or the specified-pair reading. All four measurements clear 4.5:1 with margin. Source corroborates (marketing.css:5107 and :5115 carry exactly these colours with the R3 rationale comment, and no later rule overrides either selector's colour).

Two things I checked because they looked suspicious and both cleared: the identical caption ink-pixel counts across viewports (explained by identical 12px rasterisation of the same centred string), and whether the r5 scratch .ts files would re-break tsc (they will not — R2 landed: tsconfig exclude is ["node_modules", "test-output"] and test-output/r3 is gone). Housekeeping verified: server was :3007 only, and port 3007 now has no listener. I made no writes to the worktree — all my scratch files live in the session scratchpad and require pngjs by absolute path.

No blockers. The UI gate passes at both viewports. One process note for the lead, not a blocker: the driver reported a curl step it did not log, so future rounds should require the branch-build proof be captured to a file like every other command.

verdicts.item: R4 (low) — wrap TenantLogo's no-logo fallback in <span role="img" aria-label={imgAlt}> without changing the BrandMark API
verdicts.evidence: The diff shows the wrapper added strictly inside the else arm of `branding?.logoUrl ? : `. I specifically hunted the 'aria wrapper duplicates the name when a tenant logo exists' hazard and REFUTED it: the ternary is exclusive, so a tenant with a logoUrl renders only the path and never reaches the wrapper. BrandMark.tsx has no signature change (BrandMarkProps still size/className/tone). I checked all three call sites (app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx:1309 and :1359, app/(dashboard)/invoices/[id]/page.tsx:2318) — all pass className="h-8 w-8" into a flex parent, and all three set showName, which does announce the name twice (role=img label plus the visible {displayName}); I verified against the base file that this double-announce is byte-identical to the pre-change `` + showName behaviour, so it is pre-existing and not an R4 regression. Gates: `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0, `npx jest --silent` 42 suites / 338 tests passed exit 0, `npx prettier --check` on all five touched files (globals.css included) 'All matched files use Prettier code style!' exit 0.

newHazards.summary: R3 repaired two labels but left a third element in the SAME diagram below AA. `.rf-marketing .connection-center span` is `color: #697b94` at 0.8rem (0.75rem under @media max-width:480 at :3296, which changes font-size only — I confirmed by awk that no later rule overrides the colour). Its card ground is `.connection-center` background #ffffffdb (:8646) composited over the #eeedf2 diagram = #fdfcfd, giving 4.22:1 (4.32:1 even on pure white) — below the 4.5:1 AA floor for normal text. This value is new-in-branch: the port replaced the previous 407-line marketing.css wholesale, so nothing upstream is being preserved here. It is outside R3's stated two-selector scope, which is why I am not blocking on it, but it is the identical defect class one element away and the lead should fold a same-hue darkening into the close-out rather than discover it in an owner visual review.

The R4 wrapper silently moved `shrink-0` off the flex item. Before, the `` was the direct child of the flex parent and carried `${className} shrink-0`; now the wrapping `` is the flex item (default flex-shrink:1) while `shrink-0` rides on the inner , where it is inert because the span is not a flex container. All three call sites are flex rows/columns (dashboard layout.tsx:1309 collapsed sidebar, :1359 mobile aside w-64 max-w-[82%], invoices page 2318). In practice the sibling name span uses `truncate` (overflow:hidden makes its min-width resolve to 0) so it absorbs the shrink first, and the fixed h-8 w-8 img would overflow rather than scale — so I could not construct an actual squashed render. But the explicit guard the base had is gone. One-word fix: move `shrink-0` onto the span.

No test file for TenantLogo exists anywhere in the repo (`find . -name 'TenantLogo*test*'` outside node_modules returns nothing; components/ holds only TenantLogo.tsx). That is precisely why the round-4 accessible-name regression shipped undetected, and the R4 fix now ships with no regression guard of its own — BrandMark.test.tsx covers BrandMark's classes but never renders TenantLogo, so the exclusive ternary, the role="img"/aria-label wrapper, and the tenant-logo path are all untested. A short RTL spec asserting getByRole('img', { name }) in both branches would close the loop; worth a close-out row rather than another round.

review.reasoning:
Refute-first, and every claim in the W5 report was re-derived rather than accepted. R1 R2 R3 R4 are all FIXED; nothing regressed.

The two claims most worth attacking both survived. First, R1's byte-identity: an empty-looking `git diff` is weak evidence, so I measured the diff at 0 bytes, matched the sha256 against the pin constant I read myself out of marketing-port.static.test.ts, re-ran the T7 test (56/56 green), and confirmed `grep brand-mark app/globals.css` exits 1. I then went one step past the ruling and checked whether the surviving `brand-mark--light` hook is actually load-bearing or now-dead decoration: `.rf-marketing .brand-mark:not(.brand-mark--light)` really exists at marketing.css:9711, it is the only reference to the class, and none of the eleven `.rf-marketing .brand-mark` rules declares `filter` — so Tailwind's `brightness-0 invert` is unopposed and the BrandMark comment is factually true, not aspirational.

Second, R3's ground. The whole ruling rests on #eeedf2 being what is really painted, so I wrote a comment-aware brace-depth parser over the 9,829-line stylesheet instead of eyeballing indentation. marketing.css:8642 is depth 1 with an empty enclosing stack — genuinely top-level — and it is the last of three same-specificity background declarations, so it beats #edf3fb8c (:5088) and #f4f7fc (:1323) by source order everywhere. I also confirmed the two responsive rules (:2939, :3287/:3290) touch only max-width, padding and font-size, so the ground never shifts by viewport. My own WCAG implementation then reproduced W5's table exactly: 7.69:1 and 6.46:1 on #eeedf2, hue drift under 2 degrees. This independently corroborates the UI judge, who measured the same two values off the pixels by a different route.

I disproved two of the three hazards the brief asked me to hunt. The tsconfig exclude hides nothing real — `--showConfig` gives a 478-file program still containing the marketing static test, 39 e2e specs and 42 component tests, with zero test-output files in it, and the repo contains exactly one gitignored directory by that name holding only r4/r5 Playwright scratch. The aria wrapper cannot duplicate a name when a tenant logo exists, because the ternary is exclusive and the wrapper lives only in the no-logo arm; the double-announce that does occur under `showName` is byte-identical to the pre-change behaviour, so it is not an R4 regression. The colour change likewise does not leak: only the two ruled selectors moved, and every neighbouring `.connection-*` element carries an explicit colour (svg #676d7a at :8654, strong #665976 at :8651, span #697b94 at :1359), so nothing picks the new value up through currentColor.

The third hazard hunt did turn something up, from the opposite direction: not leakage but an element left behind. `.connection-center span` sits at 4.22:1 on its composited card ground, inside the very diagram R3 just repaired twice. It is new-in-branch and it is the same defect class, but it is outside the ruling's two-selector scope and the lead's round-5 brief is explicit about scope, so I am recording it for the close-out rather than spending a round on a one-line colour change. The two TenantLogo notes are similarly cheap and non-blocking — a misplaced `shrink-0` I could not make misrender, and the absence of any TenantLogo spec, which is the process reason the round-4 a11y defect escaped in the first place.

Gates re-run by me, not quoted: tsc exit 0, jest 42 suites / 338 tests exit 0, the T7 pin suite 56/56 exit 0, prettier --check clean across all five touched files including globals.css. The worktree discipline held — HEAD is still 5ddec78e, no new commits, no stash change, and I made no writes. Land, with the three hazards carried into the close-out.
